"""Worker_Summary of the File_Sink_Worker (Event_Path, Spark aggregations only).

Input is the delivery Audit_Log DataFrame (``tenant_id``, ``destination_id``, ``decision``).
Rows with decision ``delivered`` and ``dead-lettered`` are counted. Other decisions (for example
``dropped``) are ignored. Output is non-negative integer counters, in total and per
(tenant_id, destination_id), written with Spark as JSON Lines. No event row is collected.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from pyspark.sql import Column, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

DECISION_DELIVERED = "delivered"
DECISION_DEAD_LETTERED = "dead-lettered"

SCOPE_TOTAL = "total"
SCOPE_TENANT_DESTINATION = "tenant_destination"
SUMMARY_COLUMNS = ("scope", "tenant_id", "destination_id", "delivered", "dead_lettered")

WORKER_SUMMARY_DIR = "worker_summary"


def _optional(df: DataFrame, name: str) -> Column:
    return F.col(name).cast("string") if name in df.columns else F.lit(None).cast("string")


def build_worker_summary(audit_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    """Return the Worker_Summary DataFrame (columns ``SUMMARY_COLUMNS``)."""
    rows = audit_df.select(
        F.lower(_optional(audit_df, "tenant_id")).alias("tenant_id"),
        _optional(audit_df, "destination_id").alias("destination_id"),
        _optional(audit_df, "decision").alias("decision"),
    )

    def count_of(decision: str) -> Column:
        hit = F.when(F.col("decision") == F.lit(decision), F.lit(1)).otherwise(F.lit(0))
        return F.coalesce(F.sum(hit), F.lit(0)).cast("long")

    aggs = [count_of(DECISION_DELIVERED).alias("delivered"), count_of(DECISION_DEAD_LETTERED).alias("dead_lettered")]
    per_key = (
        rows.where(F.col("decision").isin(DECISION_DELIVERED, DECISION_DEAD_LETTERED))
        .groupBy("tenant_id", "destination_id")
        .agg(*aggs)
        .select(F.lit(SCOPE_TENANT_DESTINATION).alias("scope"), "tenant_id", "destination_id", "delivered", "dead_lettered")
    )
    total = rows.agg(*aggs).select(
        F.lit(SCOPE_TOTAL).alias("scope"),
        F.lit(None).cast("string").alias("tenant_id"),
        F.lit(None).cast("string").alias("destination_id"),
        "delivered",
        "dead_lettered",
    )
    return total.unionByName(per_key).select(*SUMMARY_COLUMNS)


def worker_summary_path(output_root: str | Path) -> str:
    return str(Path(output_root) / WORKER_SUMMARY_DIR)


def write_worker_summary(summary_df: DataFrame, output_root: str | Path) -> None:
    """Write the aggregated summary as one JSON Lines part file under ``<output_root>/worker_summary``."""
    (
        summary_df.select(*SUMMARY_COLUMNS)
        .coalesce(1)
        .write.mode("overwrite")
        .option("ignoreNullFields", "false")
        .json(worker_summary_path(output_root))
    )

"""Static AST scan of the Event_Path modules (Req 11.11, 11.12, 11.13).

Bans on the event path: pandas / pyarrow imports, collect/toPandas/take/head
calls, Python UDFs (udf, pandas_udf, mapInPandas, applyInPandasWithState)
and eval/exec. Only config_model.py is exempt (it is not in the scan list).
"""
import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

PKG_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "event_forwarding"

EVENT_PATH_MODULES = [
    "pipeline.py",
    "isolation_guard.py",
    "kafka_publish.py",
    "audit_spark.py",
    "summary_spark.py",
    "envelope_schema.py",
    "sink_transform.py",
    "file_sink_write.py",
    "audit_worker.py",
    "summary_worker.py",
    "cli_spark.py",
    "cli_file_sink_worker.py",
]
ALLOW_LISTED = {"config_model.py"}

BANNED_IMPORT_ROOTS = {"pandas", "pyarrow"}
BANNED_METHOD_CALLS = {"collect", "toPandas", "take", "head"}
BANNED_UDF_NAMES = {"udf", "pandas_udf", "mapInPandas", "applyInPandasWithState"}
BANNED_BUILTIN_CALLS = {"eval", "exec"}


def scan_source(source: str, filename: str = "<snippet>") -> list[str]:
    """Return a list of violation descriptions found in the source."""
    tree = ast.parse(source, filename=filename)
    found: list[str] = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        line = getattr(node, "lineno", 0)
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for alias in node.names:
                if alias.name.split(".")[0] in BANNED_IMPORT_ROOTS:
                    found.append(f"{filename}:{line} import {alias.name}")
                if alias.name.split(".")[-1] in BANNED_UDF_NAMES:
                    found.append(f"{filename}:{line} import {alias.name}")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if (node.module or "").split(".")[0] in BANNED_IMPORT_ROOTS:
                found.append(f"{filename}:{line} from {node.module} import")
            for alias in node.names:
                if alias.name in BANNED_UDF_NAMES or alias.name in BANNED_IMPORT_ROOTS:
                    found.append(f"{filename}:{line} import {alias.name}")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            func = node.func
            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in BANNED_METHOD_CALLS:
                found.append(f"{filename}:{line} call .{func.attr}()")
            elif isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in BANNED_BUILTIN_CALLS:
                found.append(f"{filename}:{line} call {func.id}()")
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id in BANNED_UDF_NAMES:
            found.append(f"{filename}:{line} use of {node.id}")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr in BANNED_UDF_NAMES:
            found.append(f"{filename}:{line} use of .{node.attr}")
    return found


def existing_modules() -> list[Path]:
    return [
        PKG_DIR / name
        for name in EVENT_PATH_MODULES
        if name not in ALLOW_LISTED and (PKG_DIR / name).is_file()
    ]


def test_module_list_is_not_empty():
    assert existing_modules(), "no Event_Path module found to scan"


def test_event_path_modules_have_no_banned_constructs():
    violations: list[str] = []
    for path in existing_modules():
        violations += scan_source(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), path.name)
    assert not violations, "banned constructs on the Event_Path:\n" + "\n".join(violations)


def test_config_model_is_the_only_allow_listed_module():
    assert ALLOW_LISTED == {"config_model.py"}
    assert not ALLOW_LISTED & set(EVENT_PATH_MODULES)

I'm designing a `log_util.py` module with a `get_logger` helper that namespaces loggers under "event_forwarding" and a `configure_logging` function for CLI entry points to set up stderr-based basicConfig formatting, keeping library code free of handler configuration. I'm also working out how to get counts using a filtered summary query rather than collecting the full data.

For extracting batch-level counts, I'm weighing whether `.first()` on an aggregate summary row counts as violating the no-row-iteration rule -- I conclude it doesn't, since it's pulling a single aggregate counter rather than event-level data, which keeps it consistent with the spec that driver-side numbers should only ever be counters, never raw event rows.

My decision: per-batch, log the batch id, duration, violation counts (already tracked via audit), and destination write/dead-letter outcomes since those are known from the driver loop without extra jobs. """Logging helpers shared by the processing job, the File_Sink_Worker and the CLIs.

Library modules only get a logger. Handlers are configured once, by the CLIs (``configure_logging``)
or by pytest (``log_cli`` in pytest.ini). Log lines carry ids, paths and counters, never event
payloads or secret values (same rule as the Audit_Log).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LOGGER_ROOT = "event_forwarding"
LOG_FORMAT = "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s"


def get_logger(name: str) -> logging.Logger:
    """Logger under the package root, for example ``event_forwarding.pipeline``."""
    short = name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    return logging.getLogger(f"{LOGGER_ROOT}.{short}")


def configure_logging(level: int = logging.INFO) -> None:
    """Send package logs to stderr. Quiets the py4j bridge, which logs every call at INFO."""
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter(LOG_FORMAT))
    root = logging.getLogger(LOGGER_ROOT)
    root.handlers[:] = [handler]
    root.setLevel(level)
    root.propagate = False
    logging.getLogger("py4j").setLevel(logging.WARNING)


def read_total_counters(summary_dir: str | Path) -> dict | None:
    """Counters of the ``scope = "total"`` row of a written summary, or None when absent.

    The summary is a small aggregate file written by Spark (one row per tenant and destination
    plus the total). Reading it on the driver reads counters, never event rows.
    """
    directory = Path(summary_dir)
    if not directory.is_dir():
        return None
    for part in sorted(directory.glob("part-*.json")):
        for line in part.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            row = json.loads(line)
            if row.get("scope") == "total":
                return {k: v for k, v in row.items() if k not in ("scope", "tenant_id", "destination_id")}
    return None

I'm planning the generated data, config, and run artifacts to live under tests/end_to_end/run/ (gitignored, never committed), with the generator script and start script (run-end-to-end.ps1) sitting at the top level of tests/end_to_end/.

Now I'm sketching the actual test data design: 10 deterministic tenant UUIDs via uuid5 with fixed seeds, counts of 1000 matched/150 unmatched/20 bad records across 5 files, and per-tenant config rules that vary which fields get extracted to which destination files, including edge cases like tenants with disabled rules, tenants with destinations but no rules, and tenants with nothing configured at all — plus mapping out the matching keys across tenant/product/schema combinations.

I'm working out the distribution logic — 1000 matched events round-robin across 11 valid matching keys (91 each for the first 10, 90 for the last), 150 unmatched events spread across all the non-matching tenant/product/schema combos (disabled rules, missing configs, wrong schemas), and 20 bad lines cycled evenly across five failure categories like malformed JSON, invalid tenant IDs, missing envelope fields, and non-object data — while also figuring out the exact data pattern for valid events (sequential order IDs and computed amounts).

I'm settling on deterministic but varied payload fields per event type (purchase amounts, alert risk scores, login results alternating), using a seeded shuffle for line ordering so it's reproducible yet looks random, and defining event IDs as run_id plus a zero-padded sequence number. The test will need to reconstruct the exact expected output by replaying the generator's manifest and comparing payloads as a multiset across destination directories.

For the rejected file check, since each run uses a fresh temp directory, every rejected row in that root belongs to the current run, so I can just match malformed lines directly by their raw text against expected reasons without needing to filter by run id.

The trickier issue is old messages from previous e2e runs leaking into this run's output because tenants and destination IDs are deterministic. That means stale tenant-A/B messages could reference destinations not defined in the current config, triggering isolation_violation and landing in the DLQ — so the test should check that the DLQ contains nothing from this run rather than asserting violations==0, though this does mean we're polluting the DLQ and logs each run. I also need to consider the reverse case: 12.1 runs might now pick up leftover e2e messages with unknown destinations too, causing violations there, though since 12.1 doesn't assert on violation counts that may be tolerable.

I'm weighing whether to add an optional `starting_offsets` parameter to `run_worker` (defaulting to "earliest") so tests can pass explicit offsets to only read new messages, since Spark's startingOffsets works fine with a fresh checkpoint. This feels like a minimal, backwards-compatible change worth making even though the user previously opted for fixed topics with test-side filtering rather than modifying topic names — offsets are a different lever, separate from that earlier decision, and I want to keep the change reversible and clearly documented, though I don't think it's strictly necessary to apply the same fix to 12.1.

I'm also thinking about where generated artifacts land under a run-specific directory, and flagging that Windows has a MAX_PATH limit that could be a problem given how deep Spark's staging paths get nested.

I don't think runs should be automatically deleted since the whole point of using file paths is letting users inspect the output afterward — I'll just keep accumulating runs by id and mention this behavior rather than adding cleanup logic. args.text:
"""Landing-zone generator for the end-to-end run (task 13.1). Not Event_Path code.

Writes, for one run: a config for 10 tenants, 1,170 landing-zone lines in 5 JSONL files
(1,000 matched, 150 unmatched, 20 bad), and ``expected.json`` with what the pipeline must output.

Rules of the generated config:

    T0..T3  sales/purchase  include [order_id, amount] (drops internal_note)  -> dest-tN-file
            security/alert  constant region = "eu"                           -> dest-tN-file
    T4, T5  sales/purchase  all fields                                       -> dest-tN-file
    T6      sales/purchase  all fields, fan-out to two destinations          -> dest-t6-file-a, dest-t6-file-b
    T7      sales/purchase  enabled: false                                   -> dest-t7-file (never written)
    T8      no rule, one destination                                         -> dest-t8-file (never written)
    T9      no rule, no destination
    identity/login is never forwarded.

Pattern: matched events go round-robin over the 11 enabled (tenant, product, schema) keys, and
unmatched events round-robin over the keys without an enabled rule, so the expected count per
destination follows from the counts. Field values come from the event number ``n`` plus a seeded
random amount and note. Line order is shuffled with the fixed seed before splitting into files.

Run by hand:  .\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m tests.end_to_end.generator
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import random
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from tests.end_to_end import settings as s

PURCHASE_INCLUDE = ["order_id", "amount"]
REGION = {"region": "eu"}


@dataclass
class Run:
    run_id: str
    run_dir: Path
    paths: dict[str, Path]
    config: dict
    # destination_id -> list of expected output lines (event_id, product, schema, tenant_id, payload)
    expected_files: dict[str, list[dict]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # expected Rejected_Output: (line, reason)
    expected_rejected: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    unmatched_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def build_config(paths: dict[str, Path]) -> dict:
    t = [s.tenant_id(i) for i in range(s.TENANT_COUNT)]
    destinations, rules = [], []

    def dest(dest_id: str, tenant: str) -> None:
        destinations.append({"id": dest_id, "tenant_id": tenant, "kind": "file", "format": "jsonl"})

    for i in range(4):
        dest(f"dest-t{i}-file", t[i])
        rules.append({"tenant_id": t[i], "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase", "enabled": True,
                      "include_fields": PURCHASE_INCLUDE, "destinations": [f"dest-t{i}-file"]})
        rules.append({"tenant_id": t[i], "product": "security", "schema": "alert", "enabled": True,
                      "constant_fields": dict(REGION), "destinations": [f"dest-t{i}-file"]})
    for i in (4, 5):
        dest(f"dest-t{i}-file", t[i])
        rules.append({"tenant_id": t[i], "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase", "enabled": True,
                      "destinations": [f"dest-t{i}-file"]})
    dest("dest-t6-file-a", t[6])
    dest("dest-t6-file-b", t[6])
    rules.append({"tenant_id": t[6], "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase", "enabled": True,
                  "destinations": ["dest-t6-file-a", "dest-t6-file-b"]})
    dest("dest-t7-file", t[7])
    rules.append({"tenant_id": t[7], "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase", "enabled": False,
                  "destinations": ["dest-t7-file"]})
    dest("dest-t8-file", t[8])

    return {
        "kafka": {"bootstrap_servers": s.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS},
        "output_root": str(paths["out"]),
        "audit_root": str(paths["audit"]),
        "rejected_root": str(paths["rejected"]),
        "destinations": destinations,
        "rules": rules,
    }


def _shape(rule: dict, data: dict) -> dict:
    """Expected payload of ``data`` under ``rule`` (include list, then constants)."""
    include = rule.get("include_fields")
    payload = {k: data[k] for k in include if k in data} if include else dict(data)
    payload.update(rule.get("constant_fields") or {})
    return payload


def _data(product: str, n: int, rng: random.Random) -> dict:
    if product == "sales":
        return {"order_id": f"o{n}", "amount": rng.randint(1, 500), "internal_note": f"private-{rng.randint(0, 9999)}"}
    if product == "security":
        return {"alert_id": f"a{n}", "risk": n % 10}
    return {"user": f"u{n % 20}", "result": "success" if n % 2 == 0 else "failure"}


def _bad_lines(run_id: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """BAD_LINES lines cycling over five defects, each with its expected rejection reason."""
    good_tenant = s.tenant_id(0)
    makers = [
        lambda i: (f'{{"event_id":"{run_id}-bad-{i}","product":"sales","schema":"purchase"', "malformed_json"),
        lambda i: (json.dumps({"event_id": f"{run_id}-bad-{i}", "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase",
                               "tenant_id": "", "data": {"order_id": "x"}}), "invalid_tenant_id"),
        lambda i: (json.dumps({"event_id": f"{run_id}-bad-{i}", "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase",
                               "tenant_id": "not-a-uuid", "data": {"order_id": "x"}}), "invalid_tenant_id"),
        lambda i: (json.dumps({"event_id": f"{run_id}-bad-{i}", "product": "sales",
                               "tenant_id": good_tenant, "data": {"order_id": "x"}}), "missing_envelope_field"),
        lambda i: (json.dumps({"event_id": f"{run_id}-bad-{i}", "product": "sales", "schema": "purchase",
                               "tenant_id": good_tenant, "data": [1, 2, 3]}), "invalid_data"),
    ]
    return [makers[i % len(makers)](i) for i in range(s.BAD_LINES)]


def generate(run_dir: Path | None = None, run_id: str | None = None) -> Run:
    run_id = run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
    run_dir = Path(run_dir) if run_dir else s.RUNS_DIR / run_id
    paths = s.run_paths(run_dir)
    paths["landing"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    rng = random.Random(s.SEED)

    config = build_config(paths)
    run = Run(run_id, run_dir, paths, config)
    enabled = [r for r in config["rules"] if r["enabled"]]
    enabled_keys = {(r["tenant_id"], r["product"], r["schema"]) for r in enabled}
    all_keys = [(s.tenant_id(i), p, sc) for i in range(s.TENANT_COUNT) for p, sc in s.PRODUCT_SCHEMAS]
    matched_keys = [k for k in all_keys if k in enabled_keys]
    unmatched_keys = [k for k in all_keys if k not in enabled_keys]

    lines: list[str] = []
    n = 0
    for count, keys in ((s.MATCHED_EVENTS, matched_keys), (s.UNMATCHED_EVENTS, unmatched_keys)):
        for i in range(count):
            tenant, product, schema = keys[i % len(keys)]
            event = {"event_id": f"{run_id}-{n:05d}", "product": product, "schema": schema,
                     "tenant_id": tenant, "data": _data(product, n, rng)}
            lines.append(json.dumps(event))
            rules = [r for r in enabled if (r["tenant_id"], r["product"], r["schema"]) == (tenant, product, schema)]
            if not rules:
                run.unmatched_ids.append(event["event_id"])
            for rule in rules:
                for dest_id in rule["destinations"]:
                    run.expected_files.setdefault(dest_id, []).append(
                        {"event_id": event["event_id"], "product": product, "schema": schema,
                         "tenant_id": tenant, "payload": _shape(rule, event["data"])}
                    )
            n += 1

    run.expected_rejected = _bad_lines(run_id)
    lines.extend(line for line, _ in run.expected_rejected)
    rng.shuffle(lines)

    size = -(-len(lines) // s.LANDING_FILES)
    for f in range(s.LANDING_FILES):
        chunk = lines[f * size:(f + 1) * size]
        (paths["landing"] / f"events-{f + 1}.jsonl").write_text("\n".join(chunk) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    paths["config"].write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8")
    paths["expected"].write_text(json.dumps({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "lines": len(lines),
        "matched_events": s.MATCHED_EVENTS,
        "unmatched_events": s.UNMATCHED_EVENTS,
        "bad_lines": s.BAD_LINES,
        "delivered_records": sum(len(v) for v in run.expected_files.values()),
        "records_per_destination": {k: len(v) for k, v in sorted(run.expected_files.items())},
        "never_written_destinations": sorted(
            d["id"] for d in config["destinations"] if d["id"] not in run.expected_files
        ),
        "rejected_reasons": sorted({r for _, r in run.expected_rejected}),
    }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return run


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate one end-to-end run directory.")
    parser.add_argument("--run-dir", default=None, help="default: tests/end_to_end/run/<run_id>")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    run = generate(Path(args.run_dir) if args.run_dir else None)
    print(f"run_id={run.run_id}")
    for name, path in run.paths.items():
        print(f"{name:16} {path}")
    print(run.paths["expected"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""End-to-end test through the real broker (task 13.2).

generator -> landing zone (5 files) -> run_processing -> delivery.file
-> run_worker (sink_transform, file write) -> out/<tenant_id>/<destination_id>/

The topics are the fixed shared ones. The test records their end offsets before the run, reads
only what was written after them, and starts the worker at those offsets, so messages from
earlier runs are never read. The run directory is kept for inspection (see settings.py).

Validates: Requirements 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, 4.4, 5.1, 8.5, 8.9, 8.11, 15.3, 15.11.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from event_forwarding.cli_file_sink_worker import run_worker
from event_forwarding.config_model import load_config
from event_forwarding.log_util import read_total_counters
from event_forwarding.pipeline import run_processing
from tests.end_to_end import settings as s
from tests.end_to_end.generator import generate
from tests.end_to_end.kafka_helpers import end_offsets, read_since, starting_offsets_json

pytestmark = pytest.mark.kafka
log = logging.getLogger("tests.end_to_end")


def _json_lines(directory: Path, pattern: str) -> list[dict]:
    return [
        json.loads(line)
        for p in sorted(directory.rglob(pattern))
        for line in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        if line.strip()
    ]


def _canon(lines: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(json.dumps(line, sort_keys=True) for line in lines)


def test_end_to_end_through_kafka(kafka_spark, kafka_broker):
    run = generate()
    paths = run.paths
    log.info("end-to-end run %s in %s", run.run_id, run.run_dir)
    expected = json.loads(paths["expected"].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    tenant_of = {d["id"]: d["tenant_id"] for d in run.config["destinations"]}

    config = load_config(paths["config"])  # the generated config passes validation
    delivery_start = end_offsets(kafka_broker, s.DELIVERY_TOPIC)
    dlq_start = end_offsets(kafka_broker, s.DLQ_TOPIC)

    # --- processing job
    result = run_processing(kafka_spark, config, paths["landing"], paths["ckpt_processing"])
    assert result.isolation_violations == 0
    assert result.unreadable_files == ()

    published = read_since(kafka_broker, delivery_start)
    assert len(published) == expected["delivered_records"]
    assert {r.topic for r in published} == {s.DELIVERY_TOPIC}
    assert Counter(r.key.decode() for r in published) == Counter(
        {f"{tenant_of[d]}|{d}": n for d, n in expected["records_per_destination"].items()}
    )

    totals = read_total_counters(paths["audit"] / "run_summary")
    assert totals["read"] == expected["lines"]
    assert totals["rejected"] == s.BAD_LINES
    assert totals["published"] == expected["delivered_records"]

    # Unmatched events are dropped with no_matching_rule, every one of them.
    audit = _json_lines(paths["audit"] / "processing", "part-*.json")
    no_rule = [a["event_id"] for a in audit if a["reason"] == "no_matching_rule"]
    assert Counter(no_rule) == Counter(run.unmatched_ids)

    # Every bad line is in the Rejected_Output with its reason, and nowhere else.
    rejected = _json_lines(paths["rejected"], "part-*.json")
    assert Counter((r["line"], r["reason"]) for r in rejected) == Counter(run.expected_rejected)

    # --- File_Sink_Worker, from this run's offsets only
    violations = run_worker(
        kafka_spark, config, paths["ckpt_sink"], starting_offsets=starting_offsets_json(delivery_start)
    )
    assert violations == 0

    out = paths["out"]
    written_dirs = {p.parent.relative_to(out).parts for p in out.rglob("*.jsonl")}
    assert written_dirs == {(tenant_of[d], d) for d in run.expected_files}
    for dest_id, expected_lines in run.expected_files.items():
        got = _json_lines(out / tenant_of[dest_id] / dest_id, "*.jsonl")
        assert _canon(got) == _canon(expected_lines), f"content of {dest_id}"
        assert all(line["tenant_id"] == tenant_of[dest_id] for line in got)
    for dest_id in expected["never_written_destinations"]:
        assert not (out / tenant_of[dest_id] / dest_id).exists() or not any(
            (out / tenant_of[dest_id] / dest_id).rglob("*.jsonl")
        ), f"{dest_id} must not be written"

    everything = "\n".join(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in out.rglob("*.jsonl"))
    assert "internal_note" not in "".join(
        json.dumps(l) for d in ("dest-t0-file", "dest-t1-file", "dest-t2-file", "dest-t3-file")
        for l in _json_lines(out / tenant_of[d] / d, "*.jsonl")
    )
    assert not any(event_id in everything for event_id in run.unmatched_ids)
    assert f"{run.run_id}-bad-" not in everything

    worker_totals = read_total_counters(paths["audit"] / "worker_summary")
    assert worker_totals == {"delivered": expected["delivered_records"], "dead_lettered": 0}
    assert read_since(kafka_broker, dlq_start) == []
    log.info("end-to-end run %s passed: %s", run.run_id, json.dumps(expected["records_per_destination"]))

That WinError 3 is a rename failure caused by an overly long path—adding up the nested directory segments and filename pieces gets the total path length to roughly 248 characters, which exceeds what Windows allows.

This is fundamentally a Windows long-path limitation, not something the actual product hits on Linux in production. I'm weighing options: enabling Windows long-path support at the OS level (requires a registry change and user action), or shortening the test run directory structure, perhaps by letting users override the run root via an environment variable pointing to a shorter base path like a temp directory.

The renames fail with WinError 3 because paths near 250 characters hit Windows' 260-char MAX_PATH limit, worsened by the deep test run directory and Spark's staging names. I'll check if long paths are enabled on this machine.

payload.content:
The path length is exactly 260, right at the limit, so long paths are disabled. I could either have the user enable LongPathsEnabled in the registry, or shorten the run layout by using shorter run IDs and subdirectory names—though that only saves a few characters, not enough margin once audit names grow with multiple partitions.

I think the cleanest fix is to ask the user: either enable long paths in Windows, or redirect run data to a shorter root like F:\e2e\<run_id> or a repo-root folder like e2e-run\<id>, which would save enough characters to stay safely under the limit. I should also note that the processing logic itself passed all assertions (rejected reasons, no_matching_rule, counts), so this is purely a path-length infrastructure issue, and the failed run directory and DLQ messages from this run can be left as-is since they won't affect future runs.

I stopped here because the fix needs your decision.

**What passed:** all of the processing half of the end-to-end test.
- The generated config loads and passes validation.
- The processing job read 1,170 lines, rejected 20 and published 1,090 records to `delivery.file`, with the right key counts for every destination.
- All 150 unmatched events were dropped as `no_matching_rule`.
- All 20 bad lines are in the rejected output with their expected reasons.

**What failed:** every file write in the worker. The renames fail with `WinError 3` because the paths hit the Windows 260-character limit, and long paths are disabled on this machine (`LongPathsEnabled = 0`). The failing audit path is exactly 260 characters long:

```
F:\dev_python\checkpoint\tests\end_to_end\run\<run_id>\audit\delivery\.tmp\<32 chars>\_audit_file=audit-delivery.file-0-0-272_delivery.file-1-10-282_delivery.file-2-5-548.jsonl\part-00000-<uuid>.c000.json
```

The worker reacted the way it's designed to: it dead-lettered each failed destination to `delivery.file.dlq` and stopped the batch when the audit write failed. That leaves this run's dead-lettered messages in `delivery.file.dlq`. They don't affect later runs, because the tests start from recorded offsets.

The no-Docker tests avoided this by using a short temp folder. Under `tests\end_to_end\run\` the run directory is about 35 characters deeper, and Spark's staging paths then overflow. Production on Linux doesn't have this limit.

**Options:**
1. **Enable Windows long paths.** One registry change, which needs admin rights and is your call: `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled = 1`. The layout stays as you asked, but the setup only works on machines with that setting, so it has to be documented in the README.
2. **Keep the code, config, scripts and README in `tests/end_to_end/`, but write each run's data to a short root.** For example `F:\e2e\<run_id>\`, settable with an environment variable. This works on any Windows machine.
3. **Shorter run folder at the repo root,** such as `F:\dev_python\checkpoint\e2e\<8-char id>\`. That saves about 20 characters, but the audit name grows with the partition count, so the margin stays thin.

I recommend option 2. Which do you want?

So far, everything for task 13 is in `tests/end_to_end/`:
- `settings.py`: counts, seed, tenants and the run layout.
- `generator.py`: also runs by hand with `python -m tests.end_to_end.generator`.
- `kafka_helpers.py`: the test's Kafka reading helpers.
- `test_end_to_end_kafka.py`: the test.

I also gave `run_worker` an optional `starting_offsets` parameter, which defaults to `earliest`, so the test reads only its own messages. I still need to write the start script and the README in that directory. I'll do that after your choice.
option 2 is ok write the result in the windows equivalence of /tmp in linux machine

On Windows, the temp directory path is shorter than the project's own run directory, so using a compact name like "e2e-" plus a short hex id would save meaningful path length and help avoid Windows path-length limits.

But I realize the savings are thin once I account for growth: offset numbers in filenames climb in digit count as more runs accumulate messages, which could eat back the savings within ~10 runs. I'm weighing whether to also shorten subdirectory names like "audit" or make the audit root configurable to claw back more margin.

Checking the file_sink path pattern for another delivery batch, the length estimate comes out around 240 characters, still within limits. I'm considering adding an env var override like E2E_RUN_ROOT so users can shorten the root path if their TEMP is deeply nested, defaulting to the system temp dir otherwise.

I'll document the offset growth issue in the README, suggesting resetting the broker or using the shorter path override if things get too long. For implementation, I'm setting RUNS_DIR from the env var with a fallback to tempfile.gettempdir(), building run_dir with a short hex run id, and cleaning up unused gitignore entries and leftover test output directories.

I'll put each run in `%TEMP%\e2e-<run_id>`. That's the folder Python's `tempfile.gettempdir()` returns, `C:\Users\[REDACTED]\AppData\Local\Temp`. I'll also shorten the run id to 8 characters, and an `E2E_RUN_ROOT` environment variable will let you choose an even shorter root.

The data files renamed correctly, but leftover hidden .crc files are lingering since rmtree with ignore_errors failed silently. This points to a real Windows issue with the .tmp staging path depth — while harmless for customers, it does leak staging artifacts into their directory, which is cosmetic but worth fixing by having the test only consider actual files and ignore .tmp paths.

On the production side, I'm considering shortening the tmp directory name by using a shorter UUID suffix instead of the full hex, which cuts path depth meaningfully on Windows without requiring heavier changes like swapping Spark's filesystem implementation. I'd also add logging when rmtree fails to clean up, so failures aren't silent, and consider applying the same UUID shortening to the audit_worker's tmp path for consistency, though that wasn't the one actually failing.

Now checking path length math for the audit worker's temp directory -- it's close to the limit too, so I should shorten its UUID the same way and verify the audit_worker code for where that UUID gets generated.

Found it: Spark's hidden `.crc` checksum files in the `.tmp` folder have paths over 260 characters, causing silent rmtree failures on Windows. I'll shorten the staging folder names, add a cleanup warning log, and fix the test to only check real output files.

args.text:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Runs the end-to-end test (task 13) against the local Kafka broker.
.DESCRIPTION
  1. Starts the docker compose broker if it is not running and waits until it accepts connections.
  2. Creates the topics delivery.file and delivery.file.dlq (scripts/create-topics.ps1, idempotent).
  3. Runs tests/end_to_end through pytest with the venv interpreter (-m kafka).
  The test generates a new run directory each time: %TEMP%\e2e-<run_id> (or $env:E2E_RUN_ROOT).
  It is kept after the run for inspection. The broker is left running; stop it with `docker compose down`.
.PARAMETER GenerateOnly
  Only generate a run directory (config, landing files, expected.json). No broker, no Spark.
.EXAMPLE
  .\tests\end_to_end\run-end-to-end.ps1
.EXAMPLE
  .\tests\end_to_end\run-end-to-end.ps1 -GenerateOnly
#>
param(
    [switch]$GenerateOnly
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$repo = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..')
Set-Location $repo
$python = Join-Path $repo '.venv\Scripts\python.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path $python)) { throw "venv not found at $python. Create it first (see README.md)." }

if ($GenerateOnly) {
    & $python -m tests.end_to_end.generator
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

function Test-Broker {
    docker compose exec -T kafka /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 *> $null
    return ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)
}

if (-not (Test-Broker)) {
    Write-Host 'Kafka broker not reachable, starting it with docker compose up -d'
    docker compose up -d
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'docker compose up failed. Is Docker Desktop running?' }
    $ready = $false
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 30; $i++) {
        if (Test-Broker) { $ready = $true; break }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    }
    if (-not $ready) { throw 'Kafka broker did not become ready within 60 seconds.' }
}
Write-Host 'Kafka broker is ready'

& (Join-Path $repo 'scripts\create-topics.ps1') | Out-Null

# End-to-end test (task 13)

Everything for the end-to-end run lives in this directory:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `settings.py` | Counts, seed, tenants, topic names, run directory layout |
| `generator.py` | Writes one run directory: config, landing-zone files, `expected.json` |
| `kafka_helpers.py` | Test-side topic inspection with kafka-python |
| `test_end_to_end_kafka.py` | The test (marked `kafka`) |
| `run-end-to-end.ps1` | Start script: broker, topics, test |

## Flow

```
generator -> landing zone (5 JSONL files)
  -> processing job (run_processing)  -> topic delivery.file
  -> File_Sink_Worker (run_worker, sink_transform) -> out/<tenant_id>/<destination_id>/*.jsonl
```

Topics are shared per destination kind (`delivery.file`, `delivery.file.dlq`), never per tenant.
Only the file destination is exercised.

## Run

```powershell
# Full run: starts the broker if needed, creates the topics, runs the test
.\tests\end_to_end\run-end-to-end.ps1

# Only generate a run directory (no broker, no Spark), to look at the data
.\tests\end_to_end\run-end-to-end.ps1 -GenerateOnly
```

The broker is left running. Stop it with `docker compose down`.

## Where the results go

Each run writes to a new directory under the system temp directory (the Windows equivalent of
`/tmp`): `%TEMP%\e2e-<run_id>`, for example `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Temp\e2e-718294a5`.
Set `E2E_RUN_ROOT` to use another root. The run id is printed in the test log.

```
config.yaml        generated config (10 tenants)
expected.json      expected counts per destination and rejected reasons
landing\           events-1.jsonl .. events-5.jsonl
ckpt-processing\   processing checkpoint
ckpt-sink\         sink checkpoint
out\               customer files: out\<tenant_id>\<destination_id>\*.jsonl
audit\             processing and delivery audit, run_summary, worker_summary
rejected\          rejected lines with their reason
```

The directory is outside the repository because Spark's staging paths under it come close to the
Windows 260-character path limit (long paths are off by default). Run directories are not
deleted automatically. Because of the long staging paths, delete one with
`cmd /c rd /s /q "\\?\<full path>"` if `Remove-Item` fails.

## Generated data

1,170 lines per run, shuffled with a fixed seed and split across 5 files:

- **1,000 matched events.** Valid and matched by at least one enabled rule, so they are delivered.
- **150 unmatched events.** Valid, but no enabled rule matches, so they are dropped as `no_matching_rule`.
- **20 bad lines.** Malformed JSON, an empty or non-UUID `tenant_id`, a missing envelope field, or a non-object `data`. They are rejected with their reason.

Tenants are 10 fixed UUIDs (uuid5 from the tenant index), the same in every run. Products and
schemas are the fixed set from the assignment: `sales/purchase`, `security/alert`, `identity/login`.

| Tenant | Rules |
|---|---|
| T0 to T3 | `sales/purchase` keeps only `order_id` and `amount` (drops `internal_note`). `security/alert` adds the constant `region: "eu"`. Both go to `dest-tN-file`. |
| T4, T5 | `sales/purchase`, all fields, to `dest-tN-file` |
| T6 | `sales/purchase` fans out to `dest-t6-file-a` and `dest-t6-file-b` |
| T7 | `sales/purchase` rule with `enabled: false`. `dest-t7-file` is never written. |
| T8 | No rule. `dest-t8-file` is never written. |
| T9 | No rule, no destination |

No tenant forwards `identity/login`.

Matched events go round-robin over the 11 enabled (tenant, product, schema) keys, and unmatched
events go round-robin over the other keys. The expected output therefore follows from the counts:

| Destination | Records |
|---|---|
| `dest-t0-file` .. `dest-t3-file` | 182 each |
| `dest-t4-file`, `dest-t5-file` | 91 each |
| `dest-t6-file-a`, `dest-t6-file-b` | 90 each (the same 90 events, fan-out) |
| **Total** | **1,090** (1,000 events + 90 fan-out copies) |

## What the test checks

- The generated config passes validation.
- **Processing job:**
  - It publishes exactly 1,090 messages to `delivery.file`, with the expected count per key `<tenant_id>|<destination_id>`.
  - The Run_Summary shows 1,170 read, 20 rejected and 1,090 published.
- **Unmatched events:** every one of them is in the processing audit as `no_matching_rule`.
- **Bad lines:** every one of them is in the Rejected_Output with its expected reason.
- **File_Sink_Worker output:**
  - Each destination's files hold exactly the expected lines, with the configured shaping.
  - Every line in a directory belongs to that directory's tenant.
  - No staging files are left behind.
- **Never delivered:**
  - `dest-t7-file` and `dest-t8-file` are never written.
  - `internal_note` never appears for T0 to T3.
  - No unmatched event and no bad line reaches any file.
- The Worker_Summary shows 1,090 delivered and 0 dead-lettered.
- Nothing from this run reaches `delivery.file.dlq`.

The topics keep messages from earlier runs. The test records the topic end offsets before the
run, reads only what was written after them, and starts the worker at those offsets
(`run_worker(..., starting_offsets=...)`).

args.text:
"""Export the Kiro session history of this workspace to docs/ai-log/ (not Event_Path code).

For every Kiro session of the workspace, writes two files under the same base name
``kiro-YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-<short id>``:

- ``.md``: the transcript in order: user prompts, assistant messages, tool calls with their
  arguments and results, approval prompts, and sub-agent runs (prompt, transcript, response).
- ``.jsonl``: the raw Kiro export (the session's ``messages.jsonl`` followed by its sub-agent
  files), so nothing is lost by the Markdown rendering.

Nothing is summarised, reordered or dropped. Only these substitutions are made, each replaced by
``[REDACTED]``: the Windows user name in paths, private IPv4 addresses, email addresses, and
anything that looks like a credential (private key blocks, GitHub/AWS/OpenAI-style tokens).

Usage:  .\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts\\export_ai_log.py [--sessions-dir DIR]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import getpass
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT_DIR = REPO / "docs" / "ai-log"
DEFAULT_SESSIONS = Path.home() / ".kiro" / "sessions"
REDACTED = "[REDACTED]"


def _redactor():
    user = re.escape(getpass.getuser())
    patterns = [
        # Windows user name in paths, in every escaping seen in JSON and Markdown.
        re.compile(rf"(?i)(users(?:\\\\|\\|/|%5c|%2f))({user})(?=\\|/|%5c|%2f|\b)"),
        re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----.*?-----END [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----", re.S),
        re.compile(r"\b(?:ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr)_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b"),
        re.compile(r"\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}\b"),
        re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"),
        re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b"),
        re.compile(r"\b(?:10|127|192\.168|172\.(?:1[6-9]|2\d|3[01]))(?:\.\d{1,3}){2,3}\b"),
        re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b"),
    ]

    def redact(text: str) -> str:
        text = patterns[0].sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + REDACTED, text)
        for p in patterns[1:]:
            text = p.sub(REDACTED, text)
        return text

    return redact


redact = _redactor()


def _slug(title: str) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", title.lower()).strip("-")
    return "-".join(s.split("-")[:8]) or "session"


def _text(value) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, list):
        parts = []
        for item in value:
            if isinstance(item, dict) and "text" in item:
                parts.append(str(item["text"]))
            else:
                parts.append(json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        return "\n".join(parts)
    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)


def _fence(body: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    ticks = "```"
    while ticks in body:
        ticks += "`"
    return f"{ticks}{lang}\n{body}\n{ticks}"


def _render(records: list[dict], sub_files: dict[str, Path], depth: int = 0) -> list[str]:
    h = "#" * (3 + depth)
    out: list[str] = []
    for rec in records:
        p, ts = rec.get("payload", {}), rec.get("timestamp", "")
        t = p.get("type")
        if t == "user":
            out += [f"{h} User ({ts})", "", _text(p.get("content")), ""]
            if p.get("documents"):
                out += ["Attached documents:", _fence(_text(p["documents"]), "json"), ""]
        elif t == "assistant":
            out += [f"{h} Assistant ({ts})", "", _text(p.get("content")), ""]
        elif t == "tool_call":
            out += [f"{h} Tool call: {p.get('toolName')} ({ts})", "", _fence(_text(p.get("args")), "json"), ""]
        elif t == "tool_result":
            status = "ok" if p.get("success", True) else "error"
            out += [f"{h} Tool result: {p.get('title') or p.get('toolCallId')} [{status}]", "",
                    _fence(_text(p.get("content"))), ""]
        elif t == "pending_interaction":
            out += [f"{h} Approval asked ({ts})", "", _text(p.get("question")), ""]
        elif t == "interaction_resolved":
            out += [f"{h} Approval answer: {p.get('outcome')} {_text(p.get('selectedOption'))}".rstrip(), ""]
        elif t == "sub_agent_start":
            out += [f"{h} Sub-agent started: {p.get('subAgentName')} ({ts})", "", _text(p.get("prompt")), ""]
            sub = sub_files.get(str(p.get("subSessionId")))
            if sub:
                out += [f"{h}# Sub-agent transcript", ""]
                out += _render(_read(sub), sub_files, depth + 1)
        elif t == "sub_agent_complete":
            out += [f"{h} Sub-agent finished: {p.get('status')}", "", _text(p.get("response") or p.get("errorMessage")), ""]
        elif t in ("agent_note", "session_start"):
            out += [f"{h} {t} ({ts})", "", _text(p.get("content")), ""]
    return out


def _read(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]


def export(sessions_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    workspace = os.path.normcase(str(REPO))
    written: list[Path] = []
    for index_file in sessions_dir.glob("*/.index/index.json"):
        index = json.loads(index_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for entry in index.get("entries", []):
            paths = [os.path.normcase(p) for p in entry.get("workspacePaths", [])]
            if workspace not in paths:
                continue
            sess_dir = index_file.parent.parent / entry["id"]
            messages = sess_dir / "messages.jsonl"
            if not messages.is_file():
                continue
            subs = {p.stem: p for p in sorted((sess_dir / "sub-executions").glob("*.jsonl"))}
            base = f"kiro-{entry['createdAt'][:10]}-{_slug(entry.get('title', ''))}-{entry['id'][5:13]}"

            raw = messages.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for sub in subs.values():
                raw += sub.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            (OUT_DIR / f"{base}.jsonl").write_text(redact(raw), encoding="utf-8")

            header = [
                f"# {entry.get('title', entry['id'])}",
                "",
                f"- Tool: Kiro ({entry.get('agentMode', '')} mode)",
                f"- Session: `{entry['id']}`",
                f"- Started: {entry.get('createdAt')}, last change: {entry.get('lastModifiedAt')}",
                f"- Raw export: `{base}.jsonl`",
                "",
            ]
            body = _render(_read(messages), subs)
            (OUT_DIR / f"{base}.md").write_text(redact("\n".join(header + body)) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            written += [OUT_DIR / f"{base}.md", OUT_DIR / f"{base}.jsonl"]
    return sorted(written)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--sessions-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SESSIONS)
